http_admin_ui_disabled.title: Cleartext HTTP Admin UI Disabled
http_admin_ui_disabled.description: True when the cleartext HTTP management web UI is disabled ('no ip http server'; if web mgmt is required, only 'ip http secure-server' behind an 'ip http access-class' ACL). False (insecure) means a cleartext, unauthenticated, possibly internet-reachable admin web UI is enabled — the entry point of the CVE-2023-20198 -> CVE-2023-20273 implant chain.

telnet_disabled_ssh_only.title: Telnet Disabled, SSH-Only Transport
telnet_disabled_ssh_only.description: True when remote management on vty lines accepts only SSH and Telnet is disabled ('transport input ssh'). False (insecure) means Telnet is permitted ('transport input telnet/all' or a permissive default) so credentials traverse the network in cleartext for on-path/internet capture.

ssh_v2_only_enforced.title: SSH Version 2 Only Enforced
ssh_v2_only_enforced.description: True when only SSH protocol version 2 is permitted ('ip ssh version 2'). False (insecure) means SSHv1 is allowed or the version is unpinned (SSHv1 fallback), exposing known cryptographic weaknesses enabling downgrade/credential interception. Modeled as an interpreted boolean to avoid the '1'-substring trap in 'version 2'.

vty_access_class_restricted.title: VTY Access-Class Restriction Applied
vty_access_class_restricted.description: True when vty lines bind an 'access-class <acl> in' (or Management Plane Protection) scoping remote admin (SSH/HTTPS/SNMP/NETCONF) to authorized management subnets. False (insecure) means vty lines have no access-class and the control surface is reachable from any source — the dominant initial-access vector for routers.

edge_management_interfaces_not_internet_.title: Edge Management Interfaces Not Internet-Reachable
edge_management_interfaces_not_internet_.description: True when the device's management/control interfaces (SSH, HTTPS web UI, SNMP, NETCONF) are not reachable from the public internet or untrusted networks — out-of-band or ACL/segmentation isolated. False (insecure) means an admin interface is internet-exposed, the precondition that turned CVE-2023-20198 into mass exploitation. Canonical cross-component workspace attribute.

snmpv3_auth_priv_required.title: SNMPv3 Auth+Priv Required
snmpv3_auth_priv_required.description: True when SNMP management is restricted to SNMPv3 with auth+priv (USM) and no SNMP v1/v2c community strings remain in use. False (insecure) means cleartext v1/v2c communities are still in service.

snmp_default_communities_removed.title: SNMP Default Communities Removed
snmp_default_communities_removed.description: True when well-known default community strings (RO 'public', RW 'private', and other shipped defaults) have been removed. False (insecure) means defaults like 'snmp-server community public/private' remain.

snmp_write_community_disabled_or_acl_bou.title: SNMP Write Access Eliminated or ACL-Bound
snmp_write_community_disabled_or_acl_bou.description: True when SNMP read-write access is eliminated (no RW community) or, where retained, strictly ACL-bound to authorized management hosts. False (insecure) means an unrestricted 'snmp-server community <x> RW' exists, permitting remote configuration modification.

snmp_access_acl_restricted.title: SNMP Access ACL-Restricted
snmp_access_acl_restricted.description: True when SNMP access (any retained community or SNMPv3 access) is restricted by an access-list scoped to authorized management subnets. False (insecure) means SNMP is reachable from any/untrusted source. Secondary trigger to the SNMPv3/community controls.

centralized_aaa_enabled.title: Centralized AAA Enabled
centralized_aaa_enabled.description: True when centralized AAA governs admin authentication, authorization, and accounting ('aaa new-model' bound to TACACS+/RADIUS with local fallback only). False (insecure) means access falls back to shared local/line passwords with no per-admin accountability or command accounting.

strong_password_hashing_enabled.title: Strong Password Hashing Enabled
strong_password_hashing_enabled.description: True when privileged and local credentials use strong, non-reversible hashing ('enable secret' and 'username x secret' Type 8/9) rather than reversible Type 7/0. False (insecure) means secrets sit in the running-config in recoverable form.

service_password_encryption_enabled.title: Service Password-Encryption Enabled
service_password_encryption_enabled.description: True when 'service password-encryption' obfuscates otherwise-plaintext passwords in the running-config. False (insecure) means credentials sit fully cleartext. This is only Type-7 reversible obfuscation — a secondary defense-in-depth trigger behind strong_password_hashing_enabled.

default_accounts_removed_or_changed.title: Default Accounts Removed or Changed
default_accounts_removed_or_changed.description: True when default/factory and reused administrative accounts and passwords have been removed or changed to strong unique credentials. False (insecure) means default/reused passwords permit trivial credential-based initial access. Canonical reuse attribute.

shared_admin_accounts.title: Shared Admin Accounts In Use
shared_admin_accounts.description: True (insecure) when administrators share common (line/enable/local) accounts rather than per-admin identities, destroying accountability and amplifying credential reuse. Canonical reuse attribute whose secure state is false — fires with is_true on the insecure (shared) state.

bgp_session_authentication_enabled.title: BGP Session Authentication Enabled
bgp_session_authentication_enabled.description: True when every eBGP/iBGP neighbor session is cryptographically authenticated via TCP-MD5 ('neighbor <ip> password <key>') or, preferably, TCP-AO key-chain. False (insecure) lets an adversary spoof a BGP peer or hijack an unauthenticated TCP session to inject/hijack routes.

igp_neighbor_authentication_enabled.title: IGP Neighbor Authentication Enabled
igp_neighbor_authentication_enabled.description: True when IGP adjacencies (OSPF/EIGRP) require cryptographic neighbor authentication (OSPF message-digest keys, EIGRP md5 key-chains) on adjacency-forming interfaces. False (insecure) lets a rogue on-link device form an adjacency and inject or blackhole routes.

bgp_rpki_origin_validation_enabled.title: BGP RPKI Origin Validation Enabled
bgp_rpki_origin_validation_enabled.description: True when the router validates BGP route origin against RPKI ROAs (RTR session configured, invalid-origin routes dropped/depreferenced). False (insecure) means the router accepts mis-originated/hijacked prefixes regardless of ROA, enabling prefix hijack and traffic rerouting.

proxy_arp_disabled_on_edge.title: Proxy ARP Disabled on Edge Interfaces
proxy_arp_disabled_on_edge.description: True when Proxy ARP is disabled ('no ip proxy-arp') on untrusted/edge interfaces. False (insecure) lets the router answer ARP for off-subnet hosts — an on-path adversary-in-the-middle interception primitive.

icmp_redirects_disabled.title: ICMP Redirects Disabled on Edge
icmp_redirects_disabled.description: True when ICMP redirects are not sent ('no ip redirects') on untrusted/edge interfaces. False (insecure) lets redirects be abused to steer transit traffic through an attacker-chosen next hop for on-path interception.

interface_acls_enforce_segmentation.title: Interface ACLs Enforce Segmentation
interface_acls_enforce_segmentation.description: True when interface/transit ACLs actually enforce the trust-boundary segmentation the router is meant to separate (no permit-any gaps between straddled segments). False (insecure) means ACL gaps let traffic cross boundaries the router should isolate.

unauthorized_tunnel_interfaces_blocked.title: Unauthorized Tunnel Interfaces Blocked
unauthorized_tunnel_interfaces_blocked.description: True when only authorized, change-controlled tunnel interfaces exist and creation of new GRE/IPsec/other tunnels is prevented or alerted. False (insecure) lets an attacker who controls the router stand up a rogue tunnel to bridge segments and proxy traffic (T1599 boundary bridging).

firmware_integrity_verified.title: Firmware Integrity Verified
firmware_integrity_verified.description: True when the running IOS/IOS-XE image's authenticity has been verified ('verify' / 'show software authenticity file' report digital-signature and embedded-hash success against the Cisco-signed image). False means verification failed or was never performed, so a tampered/unsigned image may be running undetected.

secure_boot_image_verification_enabled.title: Secure Boot Image Verification Enabled
secure_boot_image_verification_enabled.description: True when the hardware Trust Anchor / Secure Boot root of trust is enforcing — ROMMON and the IOS-XE image are signature-verified at every boot and the device halts on failure. False means the device will boot a tampered/implanted image without a hardware-anchored integrity check.

signed_images_only_enforced.title: Signed-Images-Only Policy Enforced
signed_images_only_enforced.description: True when device policy permits loading only Cisco-signed images, rejecting unsigned or modified firmware at install/boot time. False means an attacker who can stage an image can install an unsigned/bootkit image. Secondary trigger behind firmware_integrity_verified / secure_boot.

unpatched_known_rce_cve.title: Unpatched Known-Exploited RCE CVE Present
unpatched_known_rce_cve.description: True (insecure) when the router runs an EoL/unpatched IOS or IOS-XE train affected by a CISA-KEV / known-exploited router CVE (e.g. CVE-2023-20198 + CVE-2023-20273 Web UI implant chain, or CVE-2018-0171 Smart Install). Secure (patched) is false; this exposure fires on true. Canonical reuse attribute.

edge_appliance_patched_within_sla.title: Edge Appliance Patched Within SLA
edge_appliance_patched_within_sla.description: True when this internet-/edge-facing router runs a vendor-supported release with all applicable KEV-listed CVEs patched within the BOD-22-01 remediation SLA. False (insecure) means an out-of-SLA edge appliance is left exposed to a known-exploited router CVE. Canonical reuse attribute.

smart_install_disabled.title: Cisco Smart Install Disabled
smart_install_disabled.description: True when the Cisco Smart Install client (vstack, TCP/4786) is disabled ('no vstack', port not listening). False (insecure) means Smart Install is operational — CVE-2018-0171 (CVSS 9.8, CISA KEV) permits unauthenticated RCE / config exfiltration and a single packet can force a reload (availability DoS). Enabled by default on many devices.

legacy_services_disabled.title: Legacy/Insecure Services Disabled
legacy_services_disabled.description: True when the router's legacy/insecure services are all disabled ('no service tcp/udp-small-servers', 'no ip finger', 'no ip bootp server', 'no mop enabled', 'no service pad', 'no ip source-route', 'no cdp run' on untrusted edges). False (insecure) means any of these widen the attack surface and leak topology.

control_plane_policing_enabled.title: Control Plane Policing (CoPP) Enabled
control_plane_policing_enabled.description: True when a CoPP policy is attached and active — a policy-map applied via 'service-policy input' under 'control-plane' rate-limiting/filtering traffic punted to the route-processor CPU. False (insecure) means punted-traffic storms exhaust route-processor CPU and drop legitimate routing/management (T1498/T1499).

ddos_protection_in_place.title: DDoS Protection In Place
ddos_protection_in_place.description: True when effective DDoS / volumetric-and-protocol-flood protection covers this component (here, control-plane flood mitigation such as CoPP, hardware control-plane protection, or upstream scrubbing). False (insecure) means the route processor is exposed to denial-of-service flooding (T1498/T1499). AND-grouped with control_plane_policing_enabled. Canonical reuse attribute.

management_plane_protection_enabled.title: Management Plane Protection (MPP) Enabled
management_plane_protection_enabled.description: True when MPP is configured ('control-plane host management-interface ... allow ssh https snmp') restricting which interfaces accept punted management traffic, bounding management-protocol volume reaching the route-processor CPU. False (insecure) means management-plane punted traffic is unbounded and can contribute to CPU exhaustion (T1498/T1499).

infrastructure_acl_mgmt_access.title: Infrastructure ACL Restricts Management Access
infrastructure_acl_mgmt_access.description: True when management-plane access (SSH/SNMP/NETCONF) is restricted to authorized management networks via vty 'access-class' / an infrastructure ACL, so untrusted hosts cannot direct floods of management/control traffic at the route processor. False (insecure) means management services are reachable from any/internet. AND-grouped with management_plane_protection_enabled.

logs_stored_on_separate_system.title: Logs Stored on Separate System
logs_stored_on_separate_system.description: True when the router ships logs to a remote syslog destination at adequate severity ('logging host <syslog>' with 'logging trap' >= informational, 'service timestamps log datetime'). False (insecure) means logging is local-only/absent, leaving no tamper-resistant, time-correlatable record of attacker activity. Canonical reuse attribute.

config_change_audit_logging_enabled.title: Config-Change Audit Logging Enabled
config_change_audit_logging_enabled.description: True when configuration-change auditing is enabled and notified to syslog ('archive' with 'log config' and 'notify syslog'). False (insecure) means no config-change archive exists, so an attacker can alter config/routing without producing a change-audit trail.

clocks_synced_to_trusted_time_source.title: Clocks Synced to Trusted Time Source
clocks_synced_to_trusted_time_source.description: True when the router's clock is synchronized to a trusted, accurate time source (NTP) so log entries are correlatable across systems. False (insecure) means clocks are unsynced/untrustworthy, enabling timestomping and defeating cross-device forensic correlation. Canonical reuse attribute.

authenticated_ntp_enabled.title: Authenticated NTP Enabled
authenticated_ntp_enabled.description: True when NTP is cryptographically authenticated ('ntp authenticate', 'ntp authentication-key', 'ntp trusted-key', servers bound with 'key'). False (insecure) lets an attacker spoof time to mask activity, break log correlation, or invalidate time-dependent checks.
